# X (Twitter) discourse: using AI to find a job, mid-career and older workers

Research date: 2026-09-10. Scope: what people say on X about AI in the job hunt, with emphasis on 45–65-year-olds.

## Access and confidence

- **No authenticated X access.** `twitter-cli`, `opencli twitter`, and `xurl` are all installed but unauthenticated (no cookies, no browser bridge, no API creds). `publish.x.com/oembed` now returns **402 Payment Required**. `r.jina.ai` is rate-blocked for x.com.
- **What worked:** WebSearch with `site:x.com` to discover posts, then `api.fxtwitter.com` / `api.vxtwitter.com` (public syndication mirrors) to fetch **full post text, author, date, likes, replies** for individual statuses. So every post below marked **[fetched]** is verbatim text with real engagement numbers; posts marked **[snippet]** are known only from a search-result title. Replies/threads under a post were not retrievable.
- **Coverage limits:** `site:x.com` search is noisy — many queries returned non-X results; recruiter-side "our inbox is flooded" threads and older-worker "how I present myself" threads exist but surfaced mostly via headlines rather than fetchable posts. I did not find any fetched X post from a 50+ person narrating an AI-assisted job search first-hand — that voice lives on Substack/LinkedIn/Reddit more than X.

## The posts, grouped by theme

### 1. AI screening and age: the Workday case dominates

- **Aakash Gupta (@aakashgupta), 2026-05-04 — 10.5k likes, 109 replies [fetched]**
  https://x.com/aakashgupta/status/2051390429489422670
  Explainer thread on *Mobley v. Workday*: Derek Mobley applied to 100+ jobs, rejected from all, some "at 1am, within minutes of submitting." May 2025: Judge Rita Lin granted preliminary certification of a nationwide ADEA collective; Workday's own filings represent **1.1 billion applications rejected** through its software in the period; court discussed class size "in the hundreds of millions." Key legal point: July 2024 ruling that the AI vendor is an "agent" of the employer and can be sued directly — "the 'we're just the tools' defense evaporated." Extends to Greenhouse, Eightfold, HireVue, Paradox. Line for a reader: *"If you're over 40 and you applied to a Fortune 500 in the last 7 years, your application was probably processed by Workday. You may be in the class."*
- **Polymarket (@Polymarket), 2026-06-22 — 13.5k likes [fetched]**
  https://x.com/Polymarket/status/2069161159404421151
  "Judge rules Workday must face claims that its AI hiring tools discriminated against disabled applicants, Black job seekers, women, & people over 40." Corroborated by Reuters Legal (https://x.com/ReutersLegal/status/2069269281661915278) and Reuters (https://x.com/Reuters/status/2069154720610967560) [snippet].
- **My Value Picks (@myvaluepicks), 2025-08-28 [fetched]** — links CNN, "collective-action lawsuit ... discriminated against candidates 40 years old and over." Low engagement, but confirms the CNN framing. https://x.com/myvaluepicks/status/1961051788951650497
- **Paul Flahive (@paulflahive), 2026-05-29 [fetched]** — new *IBM* suit: "IBM's ageist scheme had been programmed into its HR screening software," Daniel Swanson, U.S. District Court (links Austin American-Statesman). https://x.com/paulflahive/status/2060351705754018184
- **Stanford HAI (@StanfordHAI), 2026 [snippet]** — first large-scale study of hiring AI (4M applications): 26% of Black and 15% of Asian applicants faced algorithmic discrimination; the systemic risk is one vendor screening for many employers. Race not age, but the mechanism (one vendor, correlated rejection everywhere) is the same one Mobley alleges. https://x.com/StanfordHAI/status/2059761486000779595
- **Will Revieu (@Seeing_Redlines), 2026-08-17 — 24.4k likes, 927 replies [fetched] — ALMOST CERTAINLY SATIRE.** The viral "our AI screener had a 100% rejection rate for anyone who graduated before 2010; HR told it to optimize for 'digital natives with youthful energy'; the EEOC doesn't accept the robot defense" post. The account is a legal-humor persona (name is a pun on "we'll review"; bio: "GC. Former BigLaw. Current bottleneck... Contributor @theredlinehq", 2k followers). It spread as if real. Useful as a cultural artefact — it went viral *because* it matches what people believe is happening — but **do not cite it as a documented case.** https://x.com/Seeing_Redlines/status/2089382498149237063

### 2. AI is pushing older workers out first (labour-market side)

- **Todd (@ToddALee), 2026-07-13 [fetched, tiny reach]** — "white-collar workers 55+ are leaving AI-heavy jobs for unemployment, not retirement." The underlying source (found via web) is a **June 2026 Center for Retirement Research at Boston College issue brief (Geoffrey Sanzenbacher)**, CPS data × Tufts Digital Planet AI-exposure scores: pre-ChatGPT, older workers in AI-exposed jobs were *less* likely to leave; after late 2022 that advantage eroded and a meaningful share of extra exits went to **unemployment rather than retirement**. A companion March 2026 survey of 1,015 U.S. workers 50+: 24% call AI a threat to their line of work, 19% an opportunity, 37% both. Strong, citable, directly on-topic for the article. https://x.com/ToddALee/status/2076662431170912703 · https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/workers-over-55-ai-exposed-181909250.html
- **GeekWire (@geekwire), 2026-02-03 [fetched]** — "You're over 50 and just got laid off from Big Tech: Here's what to do next." https://www.geekwire.com/2026/youre-over-50-and-just-got-laid-off-from-big-tech-heres-what-to-do-next/
- **Simon Kuestenmacher (@simongerman600) [snippet]** — the mirror image: firms hire fewer juniors as AI absorbs junior tasks while senior headcount holds; older workers retiring later creates a talent-pipeline gap. Relevant nuance: experience is currently *protective* in headcount terms even while screening is hostile at the application stage.
- **The Random Recruiter (@randomrecruiter), 2026-06-10 [fetched]** — recruits for banks: "~150k+ layoffs this year" but AI-engineering demand is "on a completely different planet"; cites a 56% wage premium for AI-skilled workers, 7x growth in demand for AI fluency, "39% of skills outdated by 2030." Recruiter-side framing that *demonstrable AI fluency* is the hedge. https://x.com/randomrecruiter/status/2064739374231900380
- **Simons (@Simon_Ingari), 2026-08-19 — 10.5k likes, 6.8M views [fetched]** — "Lay offs in 2002: get laid off, go home, bad day. Lay offs in 2026: [image]." Pure zeitgeist; the gag is that a 2026 layoff now means an ATS-and-AI gauntlet. https://x.com/Simon_Ingari/status/2090027751017505002

Relevant because it explains why "prove it live" (trials, probing follow-ups) is the counter-move older candidates will face too.

### 4. The counter-evidence: AI screeners *prefer* AI-written text

- **Nav Toor (@heynavtoor), 2026-04-25 — 24.2k likes, 422 replies [fetched]** — Univ. of Maryland / NUS / Ohio State study: 2,245 pre-ChatGPT human resumes rewritten by seven LLMs; when an LLM judges, it picks the LLM-rewritten version **~96–98% of the time** (GPT-4o 97.6%), even when human graders rated the human version clearer; models also prefer *their own* output over other models'. This is the single most useful X post for the article's "what AI is good at / bad at" section: it directly contradicts the "recruiters can tell, don't use AI" advice *for the screening stage* while leaving it true for the human stage. https://x.com/heynavtoor/status/2048088874686300431

  Net reading for a middle-aged applicant: the two audiences want opposite things — the machine rewards fluent generic LLM prose, the human punishes it. The tactical answer people converge on: AI-assisted *structure and keyword alignment* for the screen, human-specific voice and evidence for the read.

- **LinkedIn's own AI** (via web, X posts not fetchable): AI-powered job search live in US/UK/**Canada**/AU/IN/SG, "AI job coach" for Premium in beta; CEO Ryan Roslansky's book *Open to Work: How to Get Ahead in the Age of AI*.
- **Commercial tools (Teal, Jobscan, Simplify, Careerflow, Huntr):** essentially no organic X discussion surfaced — X talks about ChatGPT prompts and open-source bots, not SaaS trackers. Those live on LinkedIn/Reddit/YouTube.
- **Warned against:** mindless AI cover letters/resumes (Scoble/Miller, Stauffer), AI-answered screening questions, auto-apply as "slop" (Wojak). Nobody fetched was warning about account bans specifically; ToS/ban risk did not surface on X in this pass.

### 6. Age-specific presentation advice (mostly off-X, X posts were thin)

- On X the ageism conversation is about *being screened out*, not about tactics. The tactical canon (found via web, consistent across NCOA, Mac's List, Ask a Manager, CNBC): keep the last **10–15 years**, drop graduation years, drop the "20+ years of experience" opener, lead with recent tools and outcomes, keep an ATS-parseable layout — with the Ask-a-Manager caveat that stripping *all* dates breaks ATS parsing and fools no one.
- "Overqualified" as "corporate code for old and expensive" recurs; coaches advise addressing it head-on (why this role, what you miss about doing the work, comp expectations stated plainly).
- Older-worker advocacy account **@o55skills** (Over 55 Skills at Work) exists but its posts didn't index.
- Notable stat found alongside (web, not X): only 32% of U.S. employers would likely consider someone over 60 for an AI role vs 90% for under-35s; LinkedIn/AARP report says 50+ workers are closing the tech-skills gap.

### 7. Canadian voices

- Thin on X. **@ShaziGoalie, 2024-12-27 — 744 likes, 115 replies [fetched]**: "Toronto MBA with 10 years of experience can't land a single interview. Is 🇨🇦 job market broken beyond repair for 2025?" https://x.com/ShaziGoalie/status/1872761813634564519
- Now Toronto (AI replacing employees, tools not boosting productivity), Douglas College Training Group (rising unemployment as job growth lags population), CTV/Toronto Sun (youth unemployment "a crisis") [snippets]. The Canadian X conversation is about youth unemployment and immigration-driven labour supply far more than about 50+ workers.
- The Jobfather (above) carries a 🇨🇦 flag; Air Canada's 2024 chatbot liability loss is cited in Aakash Gupta's thread as part of the "AI is not a separate entity" precedent.

## Recurring themes (for the article)

1. **Two audiences, opposite tastes.** Machines statistically prefer LLM-polished resumes (97.6%); humans say they can spot and penalize them. The winning posture is AI for structure/keywords, human for voice/evidence — and never letting AI answer the screening questions verbatim.
2. **Ageism moved into the pipeline and became litigable.** Mobley v. Workday (nationwide ADEA collective, vendor directly liable) and the new IBM suit are the anchor stories; the viral satire post shows how ready people are to believe the worst.
3. **Older white-collar exits are now unemployment, not retirement** (Boston College CRR, June 2026) — the article's "why this matters now" stat.
4. **AI fluency is the recruiter-side hedge** — being able to *talk about* using AI in your work matters more than AI-written prose (Scoble/Miller, Random Recruiter).
5. **Volume automation is contested**: open-source auto-apply bots are celebrated by builders and derided as slop by hiring managers; nobody older is publicly bragging about them.
6. **"Prove it live" is coming back** (work trials, probing follow-ups) as the response to AI-generated everything — which may actually favour experienced candidates who can do the job on the spot.
